note: The current trigger layer for anchors in data/upsc-patterns.json, refreshed one anchor per day. Every item carries the source it came from; items not from a primary document must be confirmed against one before they enter permanent notes.

geophysical-phenomena.omitted: Recent major volcanic, tsunami and other geophysical developments were omitted because the available primary-source results did not establish a sufficiently direct India-focused syllabus connection.

items.title: India completes landslide susceptibility mapping
items.why: Hazard governance shifts from post-disaster response toward spatial susceptibility mapping, rainfall thresholds and district-level early warning.
items.use: GSI mapped about 4.3 lakh sq km across 19 states and UTs and issued experimental or operational forecasts for 21 districts in eight states.

items.title: Kangra-Chamba seismic activity monitored
items.why: Repeated moderate seismicity shows that Himalayan risk assessment must combine active tectonics, monitoring capacity and preparedness rather than rely on event prediction.
items.use: NCS recorded 16 earthquakes in June 2026; the Kangra-Chamba-Dharamshala region is in Seismic Zone V and has seven monitoring stations.

items.title: Magnitude 5.1 earthquake strikes Uttarakhand
items.why: A contemporary Himalayan earthquake provides a grounded case for linking plate convergence, shallow shaking, ground failure and uneven vulnerability.
items.use: A reviewed magnitude 5.1 earthquake occurred 31 km northwest of Bageshwar at 16.5 km depth, illustrating continuing seismic exposure in the Himalaya.

multilateral-groupings-and-reform.omitted: BRICS, G20, WTO and international financial institution developments were omitted because no sufficiently supported primary-source result was available in the retrieved material.

items.title: G4 calls for text-based Security Council negotiations
items.why: The G4 is shifting from reiterating claims to coalition-building for a consolidated reform model and text-based negotiations, testing whether plurilateral pressure can overcome procedural stasis.
items.use: The G4 said the reform process had produced no concrete outcome after 18 years and called for expansion in both permanent and non-permanent categories.
items.source: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India

items.title: India calls for reformed multilateralism
items.why: India has framed institutional reform as management of a multipolar transition, linking representation with consultation and transparency rather than only demands for seats.
items.use: India stated that the post-1945 order is giving way to new realities and that broad consultations and transparent decision-making are necessary in a multipolar world.
items.source: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India

items.title: General Assembly President backs Security Council reform
items.why: Reform is being connected to institutional credibility and regional representation, while the UN80 initiative exposes the distinction between operational streamlining and foundational power reform.
items.use: The Assembly President supported General Assembly-led negotiations for a more representative, transparent Council and identified Africa’s underrepresentation as a priority.
